screening_decisions.reason: Randomized controlled trial with 56 patients in intervention arm and 59 in control arm. Abstract states 'Patients were selected on the principle of randomization'. Compares thermoradiotherapy vs radiotherapy alone.
Multi-institutional observational study accumulating results from different institutions treating various tumor types. No randomization mentioned. Not a controlled trial.
Prospective randomized study with 75 patients randomized (73 eligible). 37 patients to RT alone, 36 to VHF+RT. Clear RCT design comparing microwave therapy plus radiotherapy vs radiotherapy alone.
Explicitly described as 'prospective, randomised, multicentre trial' with 358 patients randomly assigned to radiotherapy alone (n=176) or radiotherapy plus hyperthermia (n=182). Phase III RCT.

Randomized trial with 122 patients randomly treated with three different methods: Group A (endocavitary hyperthermia + radiation), Group B (preoperative radiation), Group C (surgery control). Clear randomization mentioned.
Brief abstract describing comparisons between different treatments but no mention of randomization. Appears to be retrospective or observational comparison.
Title explicitly states 'Phase III study' and 'prospectively controlled randomized study'. 184 patients accessioned, 173 analyzed (87 IRT, 86 ITRT). Clear RTOG Phase III RCT.
Review article summarizing literature and own clinical data. States 'The literature and own clinical data are reviewed'. Not a primary RCT.
Observational study of 102 patients where 46 received additional hyperthermia. No randomization mentioned - patients appear to have been allocated non-randomly.
41 patients divided into two groups (A: radiation+hyperthermia+chemo, B: no hyperthermia). No mention of randomization - small non-randomized comparative study.
Retrospective analysis comparing 112 patients with thermoradiotherapy vs 91 control patients. No randomization mentioned. Mixed tumor types.
Secondary analysis pooling data from both arms of a phase III trial, but focuses on adjuvant chemotherapy outcomes, not the original hyperthermia intervention. Not itself an RCT.
Non-randomized comparison: 35 patients treated with RT+HT (group I), 36 unsuitable for HT (group II). Allocation based on technical feasibility, not randomization.
Explicitly stated as 'Phase I study' - not Phase II or III. Single-arm study without control group.
Summary report of 1211 patients with mixed tumor types. No randomization mentioned. Appears to be retrospective series.
Comparative study of 137 patients (69 with hyperthermia, 68 without) but no randomization mentioned. QoL-focused secondary analysis.
Single-arm case series of 26 patients. No control group, no randomization.
Observational study examining prognostic factors (circumferential margin involvement). No intervention, no randomization.
Observational study of tumor oxygenation in head and neck cancer (not rectal cancer). No intervention, no randomization.
Retrospective analysis of 167 consecutive patients examining prognostic factors. No intervention, no randomization.
This is a meta-analysis/systematic overview of 22 randomized trials, not a primary phase II or III RCT itself.
Randomized multicenter clinical trial comparing preoperative radiation therapy vs control in operable rectal cancer. Meets RCT criteria.
NSABP protocol R-01 is a randomized controlled trial with 555 patients randomized to no treatment, chemotherapy, or radiation therapy. Phase III RCT.
Randomized trial (FFCD 9203) comparing preoperative radiotherapy vs chemoradiotherapy with 733 patients. Phase III RCT.
Observational study comparing operative vs non-operative treatment based on clinical response. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Single-institution consecutive series reporting outcomes after total mesorectal excision. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Study focuses on cervical cancer (uterine cervix), not rectal cancer. Also observational/prognostic study, not an RCT.
Diagnostic accuracy study assessing transrectal ultrasound for staging. Not a therapeutic RCT.
Secondary/subgroup analysis from a parent randomized trial examining CRM involvement. Not a primary RCT itself.
Quality of life analysis from a parent randomized trial. Secondary outcome analysis, not a primary RCT.
Retrospective review of 412 patients from Memorial Hospital. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Randomized multicenter trial comparing preoperative vs postoperative radiotherapy with 471 patients. Phase III RCT.
Histopathological study of surgical specimens. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Retrospective review of 142 cases from Massachusetts General Hospital. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Diagnostic accuracy study correlating MR imaging with pathology. Not a therapeutic RCT.
Prospective randomized trial comparing preoperative short-term radiation therapy vs surgery alone with 849 patients. Phase III RCT.
Review article discussing hypoxia as a target for combined modality treatments. Not a primary RCT.
Cooperative randomized study with 451 patients evaluating intensive macrofractional preoperative irradiation. RCT design.
Small case series of 14 patients receiving brachytherapy. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Molecular analysis of gene expression in tumor samples. Observational biomarker study, not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a diagnostic accuracy study assessing MRI performance for preoperative staging. It involves 76 patients assessed by MRI with two observers scoring independently. There is no randomization, no intervention being tested, and no control group. This is an observational diagnostic study, not a randomized controlled trial.

The abstract explicitly states this is 'A retrospective review of 325 patients'. This is a retrospective observational study analyzing prognostic factors (radial resection margin involvement). There is no randomization or intervention comparison. Retrospective studies are not randomized controlled trials.

This appears to be a review or discussion article about endorectal imaging techniques for staging rectal carcinoma. The abstract mentions 'Numerous studies have demonstrated' suggesting it reviews existing literature rather than presenting original trial data. There is no indication of randomization or controlled trial design.

This is an observational study of 75 patients who underwent planned reoperations after initial curative surgery. The study analyzes patterns of tumor failure (local recurrence, distant metastasis, peritoneal seeding). There is no randomization, no intervention being tested, and no control group. This is a retrospective clinicopathologic correlation study.

This is clearly a randomized controlled trial. The abstract states 'We conducted a multicenter, randomized trial' and 'We randomly assigned 1861 patients with resectable rectal cancer either to preoperative radiotherapy followed by total mesorectal excision or to total mesorectal excision alone.' With 1861 patients, this is likely a Phase III trial. Meets selection criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial. The abstract states 'Two hundred four patients with rectal carcinoma that was either deeply invasive or metastatic to regional lymph nodes were randomly assigned to postoperative radiation alone or to radiation plus fluorouracil...' This compares two treatment arms with randomization. With 204 patients, this could be Phase II or III. Meets selection criteria as an RCT.
